subject: Arcadia Foods — Post-incident assurance playbook and commitments
summary: Customer reported a multi-hour throughput and error-rate surge during peak traffic. Team delivered a draft RCA, defined corrective actions and owners, and agreed an exec-facing assurance playbook and cadence.
messages:
From: Lena Morris <lena.morris@arcadiafoods.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@arcadiafoods.com>, Tom Saunders <tsaunders@arcadiafoods.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Checkout failures & throughput spike (Apr 9 evening)

Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks again for taking this call yesterday. To summarize the impact on Arcadia: between 20:10–23:05 PST on Apr 9 we saw a ~4x increase in request latency and a ~7% error rate on the Redwood inference endpoint powering our checkout personalization flow. This led to degraded recommendations and a ~3.6% lift in checkout abandonment across the East region during the window.

We need: a short RCA, the immediate mitigations you applied, and a clear remediation/assurance schedule we can present to our executive team tomorrow morning (weekly cadence afterwards). Also please attach any artifacts (logs, perf traces, config changes).

Two folks from our side who should be kept in the loop: Raj (ops) and Tom (CTO).

Appreciate quick turnaround — Lena

--
Lena Morris
Head of Digital Experience | Arcadia Foods
Lena.Morris@arcadiafoods.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Morris <lena.morris@arcadiafoods.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@arcadiafoods.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout failures & throughput spike (Apr 9 evening)

Lena — thanks for the note and the detail. Sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a priority incident and have the following immediate items in flight: 

- Short-term mitigations applied (10:45–11:30 PST): throttled lower-tier traffic to the affected model variant, enabled conservative batching to reduce KV cache churn, and rolled an emergency kernel fallback on a subset of nodes.
- Collecting traces and token-level error logs now; attaching a draft RCA and the perf trace bundle (arcadia_rca_v1.pdf).
- Working with Arcadia ops (Raj) to confirm traffic patterns and replay key traces.

We will produce a one-page exec playbook with owners and a 2-week remediation sprint plan by EOD Mon (Apr 12). Jonas will lead the technical remediation and Ben will own deployment verification and monitoring changes.

Can you confirm whether the executive readout tomorrow should be 30 or 45 minutes and who from Arcadia will attend?

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Sent from my mobile

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Morris <lena.morris@arcadiafoods.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@arcadiafoods.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: Checkout failures & throughput spike (Apr 9 evening) — draft RCA attached

All — attaching the draft RCA (arcadia_rca_v1.pdf) and a short spreadsheet with the corrective actions we've scoped (throughput_corrections.xlsx). Executive summary: 

- Root cause (summary): an interaction between our recent model variant with longer average context window and an aggressive autoscaling/eviction policy caused disproportionate KV cache fills on the GPU pools servicing Arcadia's region. That increased tail latency and produced transient OOM-induced soft errors on some nodes.

- Contributing factors: long-running inference requests from a small set of high-cardinality sessions; a recent runtime kernel change that reduces per-request memory headroom; and insufficiently conservative canarying for the kernel change on dedicated pools.

Immediate corrective actions completed: rollout rollback to previous kernel (11:30 PST), temporary session affinity for heavy clients, and a short-term scale-up of headroom for Arcadia's capacity.

Planned remediation (owners & ETA):
- Technical deep-dive + safer kernel patch: Jonas Weber — ETA Apr 15
- Autoscaling policy tuning and guardrails: Kimberly Park — ETA Apr 13
- Prefix/KV cache improvements (sizing + eviction): Olga Petrov — ETA Apr 21
- Deployment verification & smoke tests: Ben Carter — ETA Apr 14

I've included sample traces in the Drive link and noted which nodes experienced elevated soft errors.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment(s): arcadia_rca_v1.pdf; throughput_corrections.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lena Morris <lena.morris@arcadiafoods.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@arcadiafoods.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Arcadia executive assurance playbook (draft)

Lena / Raj —

Per Marissa's note, please find the draft exec playbook below. We pared this down to one page for your execs, plus an appendix with tech owners and checkpoints.

Executive playbook — high level
- What happened (30s): Kernel rollout + long context sessions → KV pressure → higher tail latency and soft errors for a subset of nodes handling Arcadia traffic.
- Impact: 20:10–23:05 PST Apr 9; ~3.6% checkout abandonment lift for East region during peak.
- What we did immediately: rollback kernel, increased headroom, enabled session affinity, and throttled non-critical traffic.
- Near-term remediation (2 week sprint):
  - Week 1 (Apr 11–15): safer kernel patch validation (Jonas), autoscaling guardrails (Kimberly), smoke and chaos tests (Ben).
  - Week 2 (Apr 18–22): prefix cache sizing and eviction improvements (Olga), extended canary window and progressive traffic ramp.
- Verification / acceptance criteria: <0.5% persistent error rate over 48h at expected peak & median latency back to baseline ±10%.
- Exec ask for Arcadia: weekly 30-min sync (Tues 10:00 PT) for 4 weeks; final closure readout on Apr 25.

Action tracker (owners & immediate checkpoints)
- Jonas Weber — Patch for kernel memory accounting; deliverable: patch + test report — ETA Apr 15.
- Kimberly Park — Autoscaling guardrails doc + config changes; ETA Apr 13.
- Ben Carter — smoke test suite and synthetic load verification; ETA Apr 14.
- Olga Petrov — cache sizing plan and rollout schedule; ETA Apr 21.

I'll present this to Arcadia execs in the readout tomorrow unless you ask for edits. Attaching the sprint roster (sprint_owner_roster.csv) and the Jira ticket (SERV-933).

-Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Engineering Manager, Reliability | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
Attachment(s): sprint_owner_roster.csv

Subject: Re: Arcadia executive assurance playbook (draft)

Thanks — the playbook looks good and the timelines are reasonable. We confirmed with our execs: 30 minutes is fine for the weekly cadence and Tom will join the Apr 11 readout. Please ensure the Apr 15 patch status is included in tomorrow's slide so our CTO can sign off on the closure acceptance criteria.

We'll expect the weekly status email after each sync with the key metric snapshot (error rate, median latency, throughput) and any deviations flagged. Also attach the final verification report when complete.

One ask: can Redwood include a short post-sprint invoice credit for the customer-impact window? We can discuss amount in the readout.

Appreciate the prompt response and the clear owners — Lena

--
Lena Morris
Head of Digital Experience | Arcadia Foods
